set.approach: From North Lake, walk the Lamarck Lakes trail up as far as the upper lake. Where it forks, bear left and cross the creek, then leave the main trail about a hundred yards beyond it. Head across the hills left of the lake toward the subpeak that holds the Ladies wall, following cairns to a boulder field, and pick the easiest line through the boulders to the foot of the crag.
set.descent_text: From the top, either walk off or rappel. For the walk-off, go left (south and southeast) over third and fourth class ground to the high point of the ridge, then trend down and left along ledges to easier ground. From there, join the Lamarck Col trail or contour beneath the wall over talus and gravel back to the base. In early season the contour can be snow-covered. The rappel option starts from an anchor on the ridge a short way south of the top and runs down the wall to the base.

review.notes: The route pages for Petra, Christine and Nicole agree on the trailhead route, the walk-off and the rappel line; they share one author so counts are left out.

set.approach: From North Lake, take the trail toward Lamarck Col to Upper Lamarck Lake, then leave the col trail at the foot of the lake. Cross the stream and climb the hill to the shoulder above the lake, staying high because the lake is cliffed out below. Aim for the talus field beneath the wall, which holds a splitter offwidth in its center.
set.descent_text: There are no bolted anchors or bail points on the route, so the way off is up and over. From the top, follow the ridge toward the summit of Lamarck, then descend easily toward Lamarck Col and join the col trail in the neighbouring basin. This loop avoids the approach side, where early-season snow can make the lower slope dangerous, so parties carry their gear with them rather than leaving it at the base.

review.notes: Single route page; no counts given.

set.descent_text: This is the standard route on the peak and also the way down: downclimb the same line from the summit block.

review.notes: Area page states the South Face is the descent route; approach is a multi-day trip to a distant basin and not described to the base, so none written.

set.approach: From the South Lake trailhead, take the Bishop Pass trail past Long Lake. Cross the creek west of the trail near the next pond, then climb a gully that avoids the big moraine. Cross the moraine boulder fields to the second buttress left of the main buttress and go over a snowfield to the base. Late in the season, ice may call for boots, crampons or an axe.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the ridge top. Descend the peak's usual way: down and southeast over blocky ground to sandy slopes, then contour east between Saddlerock Lake and Bishop Lake to meet the Bishop Pass trail to the east.

review.notes: Route page gives approach and descent; area page agrees the descent is the second-class southeast slope.

set.approach: Use the standard North Buttress approach from the South Lake trailhead along the Bishop Pass trail. The route is on the buttress just east of the North Buttress, and the start is reached by scrambling over snow, talus and third class ledges.
set.descent_text: The buttress tops out on the ridge below the summit. A second-class scramble along the east ridge reaches the summit if wanted. Descend the southeast slopes, second class, back to the Bishop Pass trail near Saddlerock Lake.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms the second-class southeast slope descent. Mileages disagree between pages so omitted.

set.descent_text: Parties come down by rappelling the line, or by climbing up and right to third class terrain.

review.notes: Single route page; approach not described there.

set.descent_text: After the traverse to the summit of Goode, descend the standard second-class route to the Bishop Pass trail at Saddlerock Lake.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree the standard descent is second class to the Bishop Pass trail.

set.approach: Go around Midnight Lake on its right, climb toward Blue Heaven Lake, then contour west past small unnamed lakes to the base of the broad east face. The route starts in the recess marked by a dark water stain, in the middle of the face.

review.notes: Single route page; no descent described so none written.
